audit.whatIsWrong: Four of seven chart rows disagree across layers: phases[3].side=Skill vs win=Zed, phases[4].side=Zed vs win=Anivia, phases[5].side=Skill vs win=Zed, phases[6].side=Skill vs win=Anivia.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Zed, Zed, Zed, Zed, Anivia, Zed, Anivia — win[] already matches it exactly; the full layer matched on none of the last four rows, and phases[4].why describes Anivia taking over while its side said Zed.

The non-monotonic chart is right and worth keeping: level 6 is yours, then his first-item lethality spike takes it back, then two items and Zhonya's return it. Death Mark is 120s at rank 1 so his kill windows are countable.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors: 'Zed's shadow poke combo outranges you completely' (Razor Shuriken is 900, your Flash Frost is 1075), 'after E-marking you' (Shadow Slash marks nothing — only Death Mark marks), and 'Living Shadow gives him a free escape if you ever land a stun' (he cannot reactivate the swap while stunned).
audit.why: Riot text: Q is 900 range and thrown by Zed and each shadow; E is a 290-range slash that slows; W is a shadow that dashes out and can be swapped to by reactivating; R makes him untargetable during the dash and triggers 3s later.
audit.corrected: He wins the poke by throwing twice, not by outranging you. Your stun is what denies the swap — landing it is the punish, not the thing he escapes.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no numbers and two filler lines about Anivia's own W and R (sequencingCues 1).
audit.why: Death Mark 120s at rank 1, Living Shadow 20s at rank 1 — the two timers the lane runs on.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with both, plus the untargetable-during-dash detail that decides when the stun goes out.

edits.before: Zed wins by landing Death Mark, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Zed wins by chipping you out with doubled Razor Shurikens, then marking the egg and swapping away before it hatches.

edits.before: - Zed Death Mark: matchup-defining — The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. It governs your forward steps. - W Crystallize spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Death Mark: 120s at rank 1 — he is untargetable through the dash, so the stun goes out after he lands, not before, and the mark repeats his damage 3s later. - Living Shadow is 20s at rank 1: stun him and he cannot swap back to it.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by holding the stun for his arrival — Death Mark drops him beside you untargetable, and a stunned Zed cannot swap home.

edits.before: Zed whiffs Death Mark and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Under tower, his 3s mark becomes your jungler's free kill.

edits.before: That is Zed’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Your Q is 80 mana; his shurikens cost energy he regains.

edits.before: Your wall is your Flash — a wasted Crystallize means the next gank kills the bird AND the egg.
edits.after: Shadow Slash only reaches 290 units — spacing him is free, so keep the wall for the ult.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Zed walks straight at you.
edits.after: He leaves a shadow behind before every commit, so the Zed you are chasing is often the one already leaving.

edits.before: Zed's shadow poke combo outranges you completely at level 1-2, giving him a clear early lane lead.
edits.after: Razor Shuriken is thrown by him and his shadow at once, out-chipping you for free at levels 1-2.

edits.before: The chip-damage pattern from Q-E-W resets keeps compounding through levels 3-5 with no punish window for you.
edits.after: Living Shadow is 20s at rank 1, but he only spends it with a Q already in the air — the chip keeps compounding.

edits.before: Same poke dynamic holds through level 5 as his shadow lets him disengage from any retaliation.
edits.after: Same poke pattern through level 5 — the shadow swap pulls him clear of your Flash Frost line.

edits.before: Zed's shadow-based Q-E harass lets him poke you constantly from level 1 while staying just outside your Flash Frost range, and Living Shadow gives him a free escape if you ever land a stun. He can reset the trade with W after E-marking you, meaning you're eating consistent chip damage with almost no way to punish him back at levels 1-2. Play max-range farming with Q, hold Wall for his all-in rather than trades, and accept you're losing the poke war early.
edits.after: Zed's Razor Shuriken harass lets him poke you constantly from level 1, and because his shadow throws its own copy a single cast hits you twice. He can swap out with Living Shadow the moment a trade turns, meaning you're eating consistent chip damage with almost no way to punish him back at levels 1-2. Play max-range farming with Q, hold Wall for his all-in rather than trades, and accept you're losing the poke war early.

edits.before: Save Wall specifically to block his ultimate dash-back, not just his engage
edits.after: Save Wall to cut off Living Shadow's path, not to space out his poke

notes: Corrections: Razor Shuriken is 900 range against your 1075 Flash Frost, so 'outranges you completely' was false — his edge is that he and the shadow both throw. Shadow Slash does not mark; only Death Mark does. And a stunned Zed cannot reactivate Living Shadow, so landing the stun is the punish, not the thing he escapes — the page had that backwards. The non-monotonic level chart (his first-item row is genuinely his) is correct and was preserved; the full layer disagreed with it on four rows and is now squared with win[] and the packet. | COHERENCE: 2 chart edit(s) withdrawn — they moved the row to the enemy while leaving the phase why describing the owner winning it.
